Thymic epithelial carcinoma; thymus is outside the anatomical axes, and this carcinoma does not establish an immune mechanism.

Congenital anomalous pulmonary artery origin and associated cardiac malformations; pulmonary arteries belong to the cardiovascular axis.

Hereditary retinoblastoma affects the retina; other malignancies are separate diseases or later risks.
Defining caudal skeletal, urinary tract and anorectal malformations; reported CNS anomalies are not established as common across the spectrum.
Benign tumor of the frontal paranasal sinus; bone or nervous system damage is not inherent to the defined lesion.

Localized hamartomatous malformation of cutaneous hair follicles and sebaceous glands.

Benign perivascular smooth muscle tumor arising in dermis or subcutis; vascular arrangement alone does not establish cardiovascular disease.
Bone dysplasia with defining hydrocephalus; dental enamel abnormalities occur in 30–79%. Proptosis and blue sclera alone do not establish ocular damage.

Defined by hair and nail abnormalities, preaxial polydactyly and thin dental enamel; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
